sections.content: You know *que* + subjunctive in relative clauses with an open or imagined antecedent from B2 Unit 13: *Busco un apartamento que tenga balcón*. Rules work in the same way. A rule speaks about anyone who might ever fall under it, so there is nobody to point at, and the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive: *Los socios que deseen usar las herramientas deberán solicitarlas a la junta*. This is why legal Spanish is full of *quien incumpla…*, *toda persona que desee…* and *cualquier socio que no pague…*. When the group is real and already known, the verb stays in the indicative: *Los socios que pagaron en enero mantienen su parcela*.

sections.title: Open group and real group
rows: Las personas que deseen inscribirse presentarán una solicitud.
People who wish to register are to submit an application. (anyone who may wish: subjunctive)
Quien incumpla el plazo perderá la parcela.
Whoever misses the deadline will lose the plot. (anyone: subjunctive)
Cualquier socio que no abone la cuota será amonestado.
Any member who does not pay the fee will be warned. (anyone: subjunctive)
Los socios que pagaron en enero mantienen su parcela.
The members who paid in January keep their plot. (a real group: indicative)

items.spanish: Todo solicitante que cumpla los requisitos recibirá una parcela.
items.english: Every applicant who meets the requirements will receive a plot.

items.spanish: Quien desee inscribirse deberá presentar una solicitud.
items.english: Whoever wishes to register must submit an application.

items.spanish: Cualquier persona que incumpla el reglamento perderá su plaza.
items.english: Any person who breaches the regulation will lose their place.

items.spanish: Los solicitantes que ya se inscribieron esperan una respuesta.
items.english: The applicants who have already registered are waiting for an answer.

sections.content: English "anyone who wishes to register" uses the plain present, so nothing tells you to change mood. Ask: can I point at these people now? If the rule is for whoever may come later, use the subjunctive. Before a noun, write *cualquier*, not *cualquiera*: *cualquier socio que incumpla*. After the noun or alone, *cualquiera* stays: *cualquiera que incumpla*.
